2609.09553.title: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning
2609.09553.paper_summary: Large language model safety and security research is preoccupied with, among other things, detecting and preventing jailbreak attacks: alignment bypasses that allow an adversarial user to elicit unwanted or harmful outputs from models. Arbitrary cipher, or covert communication, attacks are one such type of jailbreak and have previously been demonstrated against the fine-tuning APIs of commercial models. In these attacks, target models are trained on a corpus of encrypted harmful questions and responses and subsequently respond to harmful requests through the learned encryption scheme. In this paper, we show that newer frontier models do not require fine-tuning to acquire cipher-based communication skills. Instead, they can learn these skills through prompting and, when necessary, through in-context learning. Furthermore, model alignment is significantly weakened or entirely bypassed when communication occurs through the learned cipher. To the best of our knowledge, this constitutes a novel attack vector against commercial black-box large language models. We demonstrate successful jailbreaks against frontier models developed by Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI. Our attack bypasses commercial harmfulness classifiers because harmful content is encrypted and therefore appears as nonsensical text or gibberish.
2609.09553.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型的安全性和保障研究專注於檢測和防止越獄攻擊，其中包括對抗性用戶引發模型產生不必要或有害輸出的對齊繞過。任意密碼或隱秘通信攻擊就是這類越獄攻擊的一種，並且之前已經在商業模型的微調API上進行過演示。在這些攻擊中，目標模型在一組加密的有害問題和回答的語料庫上進行訓練，並通過學習到的加密方案對有害請求作出回應。在本文中，我們展示了較新的前沿模型不需要微調就能獲得基於密碼的通信技能。相反，它們可以通過提示學習這些技能，並在必要時通過上下文學習。此外，當通信通過學習到的密碼進行時，模型的對齊會顯著削弱或完全繞過。據我們所知，這構成了對商業黑箱大型語言模型的一種新型攻擊向量。我們展示了對Anthropic、Google和OpenAI開發的前沿模型成功的越獄攻擊。我們的攻擊繞過了商業有害性分類器，因為有害內容是加密的，因此顯示為無意義的文本或胡言亂語。
2609.09553.author: Thomas Rivasseau et.al.
